data.text/markdown:
Digital storytelling studio

How do sequence, sound, image, pacing, and context shape a viewer's reading of an audiovisual story? Follow the facilitator's shared schedule and production brief. Numeric stage limits remain pending a matched rehearsal and human approval.

1. Prepare your story

1.1 Orient — Make, read, revise

Required / 필수. Create one accessible first cut, study how story form changes a reading, gather two independent blinded audience readings, revise a second cut, and save the common post-task. Required controls use native labels and remain keyboard operable. Data boundary / 데이터 경계. Uploads and session state are processed inside the hosted Molab session/container, not solely on your device. Nothing is sent automatically to an instructor or outside service.

data.text/html:
1.2 Common pre-task — Reason from limited evidence

Before making, explain what you would check when an automated caption sounds plausible but may miss how sound and image work together. Evidence you would seek A plausible alternative explanation What the caption alone cannot establish

data.text/markdown:
2. Make and register

2.1 Plan — First cut

Required / 필수. Use the facilitator-approved brief, source pool, editor route, export preset, accessibility support, and help policy. If any shared value is missing, record a deviation rather than silently substituting it.

3. Story form, audience, and revision

3.1 Explore — Story structure

Required / 필수. Work with story form rather than system internals. Identify one turning point, test an alternative sequence or sound role, and explain what a viewer could reasonably read differently.

data.text/html: Turning point or narrative beat Alternative sequence or pacing choice Role of sound in the story Expected change in a viewer's reading

data.text/markdown:
3.2 Exchange — Independent audience readings

Required / 필수. Create a permission-authorized blinded packet, then import at least two distinct independent readings. Two readings are the classroom minimum, never a research sampling justification.

data.text/html: Permission-approved presentation reference Media type Duration in milliseconds Caption or transcript reference I have permission to share this presentation package for the classroom audience activity.

4. Common outcome and private export

4.1 Complete the common post-task

Required / 필수. After making and audience exchange, explain what evidence you would now seek when an automated caption sounds plausible but may miss how sound and image work together.

data.text/html: Evidence you would seek now A rival account you would keep open A claim you would not make from the caption alone
Observed stage timing or schedule deviation Help, tool, source, accessibility, or disruption deviation
